v1.feedback: The shedding-as-impermanence mechanic is a genuine design choice driven by the linked idea, not a label — good. But the facial archetypes are deformed spheres with subtle gaussian bumps; at 32×64 resolution with additive blending they'll likely read as warm glowing orbs rather than recognizable faces within 2 seconds, weakening the genealogical thread inherited from s47. Increase deformation contrast (deeper eye sockets, sharper jaw taper, more pronounced nose ridge) or add feature-line edges so the silhouette reads as a head. The fallen-petal drift is poetic but risks leaving the canvas sparse after 4–5 cycles — consider a floor accumulation plane or slow fade-to-ground rather than letting shed particles simply vanish at y < -4.

v2.feedback: The three-archetype face morph (great-grandparent → grandparent → self) is a genuinely thoughtful interpretation of mono no aware as ancestral impermanence, and the gaussian-bump facial deformations produce readable head silhouettes with eye sockets, brow ridges, and jawlines — not noise blobs. However, the connection to the parent s47 (channel_nouf_aljowaysir) is asserted in labels but not visible in the form language; this reads as a fresh build rather than a continuous morph of the parent's actual geometry/palette. The particle-shedding and ground-accumulation mechanic is poetic but risks leaving the main form sparse and the canvas bottom cluttered with faded dots — tighten the shed rate so the face stays >60% populated at any given phase. Palette is restrained and warm (sepia/dusty-rose/ink-brown) which works, but bump point size to ~0.04–0.05 and pull the camera in to z≈5 so the heads fill more frame at default view.
